transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, I guess what really brought me in is that my mind just won’t stay on one thing anymore. It’s... it's getting really frustrating at work. Like, I’ll be sitting at the bench, right? And I start looking at a customer email. This one lady wanted a custom platinum setting, which is honestly a huge pain because platinum eats through saw blades like crazy. You gotta use a specific lubricant for it, otherwise you're just snapping blades all morning and they aren't cheap. 

But anyway, I'm reading her email, and then out of nowhere I notice a tiny saw mark on a completely different silver band on my desk. So I go to buff that out, but then there's this loud noise outside. Sounded like a street sweeper or a garbage truck, though they usually only come by on Thursdays. I actually watched the driver clip a mailbox once, just totally took it out... wait, sorry. 

What I mean is, I jump from the email, to the saw mark, to the noise out the window, and then suddenly I look down and I realize I’ve completely lost the whole work order. I just can't keep my head on straight.
Does your difficulty concentrating happen most of the time, or only during distinct periods when your mood is unusually high or irritable?

Well, it's definitely not all the time. It really started acting up right after this big gem and mineral show I went to last month. They have these amazing Tucson shows, people come from all over the world. I saw this one guy who had a whole table of Australian opals, just raw, sitting in water. If you let them dry out too fast they craze—like, they get all these tiny little cracks in them and then they're basically useless for setting. You have to keep them hydrated, which seems weird for a rock, right? 

But yeah, after that show, I just felt... I don't know, lit up. Like I was larger than life, totally buzzing. I had all these ideas for new settings. But then, if anyone tried to tell me to slow down, or my boss asked me to stick to normal shop hours instead of staying till 3 AM, I just snapped at them. I got so mad, so fast. It was like they were trying to put out a fire with a squirt gun, and I just couldn't handle it. I don't usually get that irritable, but man, I was just biting people's heads off if they got in my way.
How long has this unusually energized and irritable period lasted continuously?

It lasted for about two weeks, I'd say. Like, right after I got back from that show—oh, I forgot to mention, I actually won a little award there for a custom silver pendant I brought. It was this really intricate filigree work, which takes forever because you have to twist these tiny silver wires together and solder them without melting the whole piece. Silver conducts heat so fast, you know? You have to be super careful with the torch. I use this little Smith Little Torch, it's great for fine work, uses oxygen and propane. 

Anyway, yeah, right after that award, that's when the whole wired, out-of-control stretch started. I just couldn't turn it off for those two weeks. My boss was threatening to take my keys to the shop because I was burning through so much gas and materials. But I just felt like I had to keep making things, you know? Like my hands couldn't stop moving.
Before this recent two-week period, have you ever had another distinct period when you were unusually energized or irritable and needed much less sleep?

Yeah, actually, a couple years ago I had a stretch exactly like that. I remember it because for a while I was sleeping maybe two or three hours a night, tops. But I wouldn't even be tired—I’d get up completely clear-headed and just so excited to start cutting stones or posting new designs online before the sun even came up. 

I was cutting a lot of malachite back then. You have to be incredibly careful with malachite because the dust is toxic. It’s got copper in it, you know? So if you breathe it in while you're grinding, it can really mess up your lungs. I actually had to buy this heavy-duty respirator, which was super uncomfortable and made my face sweat like crazy. Plus, it fogs up your safety glasses, and you absolutely cannot see what you're doing on the cabbing machine. The water from the grinding wheels sprays everywhere too, so you end up wearing this thick waterproof apron that makes you look like a butcher. My buddy came over once while I was in full gear and just about died laughing. 

But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, the sleep. Yeah, I’d just be up at 3 or 4 in the morning, totally wired and ready to go, setting up my light box to take photos of the stones for my page.
